theater: 筑前國博多灣志賀島海面

battle.name: 塞凡戰役
battle.theater: 筑前國博多灣志賀島海面
battle.brief: 寛平六年十一月二十五日，蒙古帝國的東渡艦隊在筑前國博多灣、即志賀島與勝連外海現身，企圖登陸九州。大宰府遣弓兵與水軍出海拒守，敵艦多數在冬季暴風中傾覆，僅數人生還被俘。此役是文永、弘安兩次元寇的先聲；卡面所選的科林斯青銅盔早於此役一千五百餘年退役，只作封閉式護頭的對照。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 塞南戰役爆發時，交戰一方是蒙古帝國的東路遠征艦隊，另一方是平安時代後期的日本。蒙古方面，當時帝國由定宗在位，攝政之權仍握在乃馬真手中，遠征軍以「東征服」的名義組建：兵員包含蒙古人、契丹人、西域漢人與高麗人，船上另有南宋沿海來的船工與水手，造船則依高麗人多年累積的造船技術與航海經驗。現存史料查不到這支艦隊的統兵者姓名、編制番號與出發港，蒙古方面的詔令殘卷亦無從查證，故此只能確認其規模是一支混合艦隊，而非純粹的蒙古騎兵。防守一方是日本朝廷在九州的鎮西體系，以大宰府（後世稱鎮西府）為核心，屬藤原氏攝政一門節制，命令由京都經驛傳下達；實際臨陣的兵力則由九州在地豪族與大宰府所領的弓兵、水軍湊成，宗像、大友、松浦一系在筑前、肥前、壱岐沿海各有勢力。朝鮮半島上的高麗此時尚未被蒙古征服，卻已被捲入蒙古的海上計劃，態度既恐懼又敷衍。
countriesEn: When the Battle of Seinan broke out, one side was an eastern expeditionary fleet of the Mongol Empire and the other was Japan in the late Heian period. On the Mongol side the empire was ruled by Güyük, with the regency of Töregene still influential at court, and the expedition was raised under the banner of the eastern conquest: soldiers and crews included Mongols, Khitans, western Chinese and Koreans, while shipwrights and sailors from the Southern Song coast served aboard; the hulls were built to Korean practice, drawing on a shipbuilding and seamanship tradition the Koreans had accumulated over decades. Surviving sources do not name the commander, the unit designation or the port of departure, and no fragment of the Mongol orders has been found, so the only safe statement is that this was a mixed fleet and not an army of pure Mongol cavalry. The defenders were the western Japanese command system centred on Dazaifu, the provincial government of Kyushu, acting under the Fujiwara regents at Kyoto; orders travelled down the post road from the capital, but the men actually engaged were drawn from the local Kyushu clans and from the archers and water militia of Dazaifu, with the Munakata, Otomo and Matsuura houses holding ground along the coasts of Buzen, Hizen and Iki. Korea had not yet been conquered by the Mongols, yet it was already being drawn into their naval plans, and its attitude was one of fear mixed with evasion.
people: 關鍵人物有兩頭都要說明：進攻方的統兵者姓名不見於現存記錄。塞南戰役的日本方面史料主要來自編年記與地誌殘卷，元廷詔令與蒙古自身的戰報在十三世紀初尚未系統保存，因此無法指認是哪一位蒙古王爺或哪一位高麗官員率船。倒是隨船的高麗造船者與宋國水手在戰後被俘，其身份在口供中被記為「新羅人」「唐人」，這是雙方唯一確定的交會點。防守一方可以確定的是制度上的主角：此時朝廷由藤原氏攝政一門把持，主政者為藤原行經一門，九州的實際防衛由大宰府負責；當敵船現身博多大津的消息傳到大宰府，鎮西府長以下依既定條例分派弓兵、水軍與早船，發令者姓名僅在殘篇中以官職出現，未留下可考的個人名。此外，九州沿岸的宗像氏與大友氏等豪族首領受召率兵赴海，事前並沒有得到「蒙古」這個國號的情報，只是依舊例把來船當作海寇處理；此役之後，負責海防的武將才逐漸開始在公文中固定使用「元」「蒙古」的稱呼，日本對北方帝國的認知，是從這裡才開始慢慢成形。
peopleEn: Key figures have to be treated on both sides, and the attackers are the harder case: the name of the commander does not appear in any surviving record. The Japanese material for the Battle of Seinan comes chiefly from chronological annals and fragments of local gazetteers, while the Mongol court's orders and the empire's own despatches had not yet been systematically preserved in the early thirteenth century, so no Mongol prince and no Korean official can be identified as the man who led the ships. What is certain is that Korean shipwrights and Song seamen were taken alive; in the depositions they are called new-ralo and Tang men, and this is the only definite point of contact between the two sides. On the defending side the protagonist is institutional rather than personal: court government at the time was held by the Fujiwara regents, with the main authority in the hands of the line of Fujiwara Yukitsune, while the actual defence of Kyushu was the business of Dazaifu. When the news that enemy ships had appeared off the great port of Hakata reached the provincial capital, the governor and his staff distributed archers, water militia and fast boats according to written procedure; the men who issued those orders survive only as offices in the fragments, and no personal name can be verified. In addition, the heads of the Munakata and Otomo houses along the Kyushu coast were summoned to bring their men to the shore, and they had received no intelligence about any state called Mongolia; they followed precedent and treated the arriving ships as pirates. Only after this battle did the officers responsible for coastal defence begin to fix the words gen and Menggu in their official documents, and Japanese understanding of the northern empire grew slowly from this point.
kits: 本卡兵器為科林斯青銅盔，鑄造於公元前六百五十年前後的希臘城邦世界，屬重裝步兵的頭部護具。必須坦白說明：它在塞南戰役現場不可能出現，到公元九二四年時已退役一千五百餘年，只可能作為東亞宮廷收藏的舶來珍玩存在。卡片讓它站在這場戰役的位置，是為了指認一種設計家族：全正面開眼、以封閉式金屬面罩換取近乎全向的視野，代價是聽覺與通氣受阻，戴盔者無法獨自判斷側後，只能靠同伴與隊形活命。真正在九二四年扛下這份工作的，是交戰雙方各自的頭盔：蒙古與高麗兵裝束札甲或皮甲，頭戴皮兜與鐵笠式兜，頸後披護頸；日本一方的弓兵則穿大具足一系的大鎧，戴鐵兜，立見與眉庇遮住面門，袖甲與草摺擋住飛來的矢鏃。進攻方的攻擊裝備以蒙古反曲弓為主，配合菱形鏃與高麗式長柄刀，射手皆為步兵；海船依高麗造船法打造，堅帆方艫，配櫓、鐵錨與淡水桶，船上無攻城器，馬匹無從隨船遠渡，這一點正是蒙古人在海灣中失去最大優勢之處。防守方用和弓與大矢近射，射手配太刀、薙刀與槍，並以早船、快艇封住志賀島與勝連的河口。兩軍都沒有動用攻城機具，也沒有任何火藥武器。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Corinthian helmet, cast in the world of the Greek city-states around 650 BC and belonging to the kit of heavy infantry. It must be said plainly: it cannot have been present on the field at Seinan, and by AD 924 it had been out of use for more than fifteen centuries, surviving at most as a curio of foreign manufacture in East Asian courtly collections. The card places it in this battle in order to identify a family of design: a fully open face, a closed metal mask bought in exchange for something close to all-round vision, at the price of impaired hearing and ventilation, so that the man inside cannot judge what is behind and beside him and must live by his comrades and by the discipline of the formation. The headgear that actually carried that burden in 924 belonged to the two sides themselves. Mongol and Korean soldiers wore lamellar or leather armour with leather or iron-rimmed caps and neck guards; Japanese archers wore the heavy o-yoroi of the daiguzoku family with iron helmets whose tate-mi and mabashi covered the face, while sode and kusazuri turned the incoming arrows. The attacker's offensive equipment centred on the Mongol composite bow, used with rhomboid heads and Korean-style long-handled sabres, all employed by infantrymen. The sea-going ships were built to Korean practice, with hard sails and bluff hulls, fitted with sweeps, iron anchors and water casks; they carried no siege engines, and horses could not be shipped across such a passage, which is precisely where the Mongols lost their greatest advantage in a bay. The defenders used the yumi and heavy arrows at close range, their archers armed with tachi, naginata and spear, while fast boats and light craft sealed the mouths of the river channels at Shikashima and Katsuren. Neither side deployed siege machines, and neither had any gunpowder weapons.
tactics: 進攻方的戰術只能從結果反推。蒙古帝國的海上遠征有固定季節：順著東亞季風由高麗、江南向東北走，返程才靠反向季風，因此出動多選在夏末秋初。九二四年的艦隊卻在十一月下旬出現在九州外海，正是季節逆轉的時段，駕船者失去順風，又被偏北的風浪推回岸邊，艦隊在玄界灘與博多灣內失去操縱餘裕。數百艘船同時擠在海灣裡，一旦起風，密集的船體互相妨礙，結果不是沉於外海，而是整片被壓進岸邊淺灘。日本一方的部署是典型的海防邏輯：先以水軍與早船封住志賀島、勝連兩處河口，弓兵在海岸列陣射擊來船、封鎖登陸點，再用烽火與早船把消息逐段送往宗像、飯塚與大宰府；命令本身由京都經驛傳下達，需要十天以上，故此役的實際指揮規模極小，多是各豪族首領各自應變。雙方真正交手並不激烈，海上的勝負主要由潮流、港口地形與天候決定，而不是陣形與武器。值得一提的對照是：此役之後日本並未立即修築石垣，築城防線要等到一二七四年與一二八一年之後才在唐津、志賀島與壹岐成真。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the attackers can only be reconstructed backwards from the outcome. The Mongol Empire's seaborne expeditions followed a fixed seasonal rhythm: outward they rode the East Asian monsoon from Korea and the Chinese coast towards the north-east, and only the return leg used the reversed wind, so departures were normally made in late summer or early autumn. The fleet of 924 nevertheless appeared off the Kyushu coast in the last third of the eleventh month, exactly when the season turns; the crews lost their fair wind and were pushed back towards the shore by northerly weather, and the fleet lost its room to manoeuvre in the Genkai Sea and inside Hakata Bay. With hundreds of ships crowded into the same water, a rising wind made the hulls foul one another, so that the result was not a loss on the open sea but the whole mass of the fleet driven onto the shallows along the shore. The Japanese response followed a recognisable coastal defence logic: fast boats and the water militia first sealed the river mouths at Shikashima and Katsuren; archers then drew up along the shore to shoot at the incoming ships and block the landing points; beacon fires and fast craft carried the news onward to Munakata, Iizuka and Dazaifu. The orders themselves came from Kyoto by post road and needed more than ten days, so the scale of command in this action was minute, each clan leader improvising on his own. The two sides barely engaged: the outcome at sea was decided by tide, harbour geography and weather rather than by formations and weapons. One instructive contrast is that no stone ramparts were raised immediately after this battle; the defensive lines only took shape at Karatsu, Shikashima and Iki after the campaigns of 1274 and 1281.
data: 可核對的數字不多，逐一列出：戰役時間是日本曆寛平六年十一月二十五日，即公元九二四年十二月；戰場在筑前國博多灣，志賀島與宗像諸島之間的早瀨戶海峽最窄處約六至七公里，勝連（唐津）距博多津約七公里，大宰府距博多津約十公里。進攻方由高麗南部出航，經對馬海峽最窄約一百三十公里的海路，總航程約八百公里，途中會失去標的與風力，需在海上待機。艦隊規模、隨船兵員、死亡與被俘人數，正史與編年記均無記載；後世常以一二七四年出動九百至一千四百艘、一二八一年四千四百艘為參照，但那兩次已是數十年後的組織動員，不能倒推九二四年，任何精確數字都不宜寫出。防守方同樣沒有留下兵力編成的記載：出動的弓兵與水軍分屬數處豪族，數目不詳。唯一有數字感的是時間：從九二四年到天慶元年（一九三六年）再犯，再到文永十一年（一二七四年）與弘安八年（一二八一年）兩役，中間隔了三百五十年；而九二四年距科林斯青銅盔定型，已過一千五百七十餘年。
dataEn: Verifiable figures are few, so they are listed one by one. The date of the action is the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month of Kanpyo 6 in the Japanese calendar, that is December of AD 924. The field of battle was Hakata Bay in Buzen, where the Hayasetogata strait between Shikashima and the Munakata islands narrows to about six or seven kilometres; Katsuren at Karatsu lies some seven kilometres from the port of Hakata, and Dazaifu some ten. The attacking fleet sailed from southern Korea by a route of roughly eight hundred kilometres through the Korea Strait, which is at its narrowest about one hundred and thirty kilometres wide, and would have had to wait at sea for wind and for bearings. The number of ships, the number of men aboard, and the numbers of dead and captured are simply not recorded in the annals. Later writers often quote the nine hundred to fourteen hundred vessels of 1274 or the four thousand four hundred of 1281 as a yardstick, but those were organisational mobilisations decades later and cannot be read backwards onto 924, so no precise figure should be given. The defenders left no record of their force either: the archers and water militia who came out belonged to several separate houses, and the numbers are unknown. The only figures that carry weight are intervals of time: from 924 to the renewed attempt of 936, and then to the campaigns of 1274 and 1281, three hundred and fifty years lie between; and by 924 the Corinthian helmet had already been out of service for some fifteen hundred and seventy years.
cause: 為什麼會打起來，蒙古一方的直接動因已經不可確證，只能給出結構性的解釋。蒙古帝國在十二世紀三十年代起以鐵騎西征歐洲，在西線受阻之後，發現高麗的造船者與宋國的沿海船工能把草原帝國的戰爭帶上東亞海路，於是把日本列為順路的下一個目標。這是一種以海路取代陸路的擴張轉向：既然在歐洲的城堡牆前屢攻不下，就試試島國的海岸。蒙古對高麗的壓力自一二三一年起持續，遠征日本的船隻與船工必然要求高麗提供，而高麗王朝此時既未完全臣服，也不願徹底拒絕，只好以拖延、稱病與奉使的方式周旋，這一點在日方記錄裡完全看不出來，只留下「唐船」「新羅船」這類帶敵意的稱呼。日本方面的起因則是被動的：九二四年的日本朝廷並不知道北方存在一個叫「蒙古」的帝國，甚至在二十多年後的一二六八年元使到訪大宰府之前，日本文獻從未用過「蒙古」這個詞。所以就當時的日本而言，這場戰役並不是國際戰爭，而是一次來歷不明的海寇入侵，被地方官府按既有程序處理。理解這一點，才會明白九二四年日本守住了海岸，卻完全不知道自己躲過了什麼。
causeEn: Why the fighting began cannot be pinned down on the Mongol side; only a structural explanation remains. From the 1230s the Mongol Empire had been campaigning westward across Europe with its mounted armies, and after being checked in the west it discovered that Korean shipwrights and Southern Song seafarers could carry the steppe empire's wars onto the East Asian sea routes, so it listed Japan as the next target along the way. This was a turn in expansion from land to sea: if castles in Europe would not fall, try the coasts of an island realm instead. Mongol pressure on Korea had been continuous since 1231, and an expedition to Japan would necessarily require ships and shipwrights from Korea; the Goryeo court, neither fully submitted nor willing to refuse outright, could only stall, plead illness and send envoys. None of this appears in the Japanese record, which preserves only hostile labels such as Tang ship and Silla ship. Japan's own cause was passive: the court of 924 had no idea that a state called Mongolia existed in the north, and Japanese documents would not use the word at all until more than twenty years later, when Yuan envoys reached Dazaifu in 1268. To the Japanese of the day this was therefore not a war between states but a raid by pirates of unknown origin, handled by the provincial authorities under standing procedure. Only with that understood does it make sense that Japan held its coast in 924 without the least idea of what it had been saved from.
impact: 直接影響分三層。第一層在戰術層面：大宰府的水軍、早船與弓兵聯動，第一次在史書上留下「敵艦抵博多大津、日本軍出海應戰」的完整記錄，此後九州海岸的哨戒節奏、烽火配置與情報上報路徑都被重新校準，雖然當時並未立刻修築石垣與水城。第二層在東亞地緣層面：蒙古帝國第一次確認日本不是可以輕易吃下的目標。九二四年之後並未罷手，一九三六年天慶元年又有一次規模更小的嘗試，於筑前與壹岐一帶被擋回；真正把一切都改寫的仍是一二七四年與一二八一年兩役，那時日本已完成石垣、鐵炮與水軍的準備，才把蒙古遠征徹底擋在九州外海。第三層在歷史記憶層面：與一二七四、一二八一年不同，塞南戰役在當時並沒有衍生出寺社祈禱、繪卷、寶物等強烈的社會記憶，長期只以編年記與地誌殘篇的形式沉睡，直到二十世紀日本學界整理元寇史才把它重新挖出來。這說明日本社會關於「蒙古來襲」的集體記憶，是從十三世紀末才開始建構的，九二四年只是被追溯時才找回來的一個更早起點。
impactEn: The effects work on three levels. At the tactical level, the coordinated use of the water militia, fast boats and archers of Dazaifu produced the first complete written record of enemy ships reaching the great port of Hakata and Japanese troops putting out to meet them, and the watch rhythm, beacon placement and reporting lines along the Kyushu coast were all recalibrated afterwards, even though no ramparts or sea forts were raised on the spot. At the geopolitical level of East Asia, the Mongol Empire learned for the first time that Japan was not a country to be swallowed easily. It did not stop: in 936, under the Tenshō era, a smaller attempt was made and turned back around Buzen and Iki. What truly rewrote the picture were the campaigns of 1274 and 1281, when Japan already had stone walls, iron guns and a water force ready, and turned the Mongol expeditions back outside the seas of Kyushu for good. At the level of historical memory, Seinan differs from 1274 and 1281 in that it produced no strong civic memory at the time, no temple prayers, no picture scrolls and no treasured relics; it lay dormant in annals and gazetteer fragments until twentieth-century Japanese scholarship on the Mongol invasions dug it out again. That in turn shows that the collective Japanese memory of a Mongol invasion was constructed only from the late thirteenth century, and that the year 924 is an earlier starting point recovered by hindsight.
result: 點到最後：進攻方全軍覆沒，但沒有一箭是日本軍射出去的。蒙古與高麗的艦隊在九二四年十一月下旬的暴風中大批沉沒、擱淺在博多灣與玄界灘的岸線上，絕大多數人隨船滅沒，現存記錄只提到少數生還者被俘，其中包含被稱為「高麗人」與「唐人」的船員；他們的供述被帶回大宰府，日後或許成為日方理解北方來客的第一手線索。防守方沒有明確的傷亡記載，但這是因為交火本身極少：敵人未能完成登陸，日軍的弓兵與水軍主要在岸上目擊並攔截沉船。從結果看，雙方都沒有取得戰果上的勝負——蒙古的遠征因海況與後勤而終止，日本的九州防衛則以極小的代價贏得了三百五十年的緩衝期，直到形勢改變的時代到來，這份緩衝才會被一筆勾銷。回頭看卡面上的科林斯青銅盔：一件公元前六百五十年的希臘重步兵頭盔，與一頂日本弓兵的鐵兜、蒙古水手的皮兜同樣說明同一件事——頭盔保護的是人，真正讓人活下來的卻是隊形、天候與潮汐，而不是任何一件被神化的裝備。
resultEn: To the end: the attacking force was destroyed, and not one arrow was fired by a Japanese soldier to do it. The Mongol and Korean fleet foundered in the storm of the last third of the eleventh month of 924, driven onto the shoreline of Hakata Bay and the Genkai Sea, and the overwhelming majority of the men went down with their ships; the surviving record mentions only a few men taken alive, among them crewmen called Koreans and Tang men. Their depositions were carried back to Dazaifu and may later have become the first-hand material by which the Japanese understood visitors from the north. No clear casualty record survives for the defenders, but that is because the actual exchange of fire was minimal: the enemy never completed a landing, and the Japanese archers and water militia mostly watched from the shore and intercepted the wrecking hulls. Judged by results, neither side won a clear military victory: the Mongol expedition ended through sea conditions and logistics, while the defence of Kyushu bought Japan a buffer of three hundred and fifty years at very small cost, a buffer that would be cancelled only when the age of changing circumstances arrived. Looking back at the Corinthian helmet on the card, a Greek heavy infantry helm of 650 BC teaches the same lesson as a Japanese archer's iron helmet or a Mongol sailor's leather cap: the helmet protects the man, but what actually keeps him alive is formation, weather and tide, not any single piece of equipment that has been made sacred.
